name: Frog Stretch
summary: A quadruped groin stretch that mobilizes the hip joints and increases flexibility in the adductors.

setup: Start on all fours on a padded mat or soft surface.
Lower your forearms to the floor with your elbows positioned under your shoulders.
Gradually widen your knees as far apart as comfortably possible while keeping your inner feet turned outward and resting on the floor.
steps: Keep your spine neutral and your core gently engaged to avoid excessive arching in your lower back.
Slowly shift your hips backward toward your heels until you feel a deep stretch along your inner thighs and groin.
Hold the position statically, or gently rock your hips forward and backward in a small, controlled range of motion.
To exit, slowly shift your weight forward onto your forearms and walk your knees back together.
instructions.breathing: Breathe deeply and rhythmically, exhaling to relax into the stretch as your hips sink backward.

common_faults.fault: Excessively arching the lower back to force the hips deeper.
common_faults.correction: Engage the abdominals to maintain a neutral lumbar spine throughout the stretch.

common_faults.fault: Spreading the knees beyond a comfortable range of motion too quickly.
common_faults.correction: Ease into the position gradually and use knee padding to avoid sharp joint discomfort.

precautions: Use a folded mat or knee pads if you experience direct pressure pain on the inner knee joints.
